'''Leslie Stephen Coles''' (January 19, 1941 – December 3, 2014) was an American biogerontologist who was the co-founder and executive director of the [[Gerontology Research Group]]<ref name=zaslow>{{cite news |first=Jeffrey |last=Zaslow |authorlink=Jeffrey Zaslow |title=Gerontology sleuths search for 'supercentenarians' |url=http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/05059/463487.stm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051220154931/http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/05059/463487.stm |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 20, 2005 |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |agency=[[Wall Street Journal]] |accessdate=December 29, 2014 |date=February 28, 2005}}</ref> where he conducted research on [[supercentenarians]]<ref name=bruin>{{cite news |title=Research group tracks oldest-living people |url=http://dailybruin.com/2004/06/09/research-group-tracks-oldest-l/ |publisher=[[Daily Bruin]] |last=Inouye |first=Emily |date=June 9, 2004 |accessdate=December 29, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Researchers look for secrets of living to 100 and beyond |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2006/12/31/researchers-look-for-secrets-of-living-to-100-and-beyond/ |newspaper=[[Baltimore Sun]] |last=O'Brien |first=Dennis |date=December 31, 2006 |access-date=December 29, 2014}}</ref> and aging.<ref>{{cite news |first=Duff |last=Wilson |title=Aging: Disease or Business Opportunity? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/04/15/business/yourmoney/15aging.html |work=[[New York Times]] |date=April 15, 2007 |accessdate=December 20, 2014}}</ref> He was also a visiting scholar in the computer science department at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Coles, L. Stephen |url=http://www.directory.ucla.edu |publisher=UCLA |accessdate=2007-10-31}}</ref> and an assistant researcher in the Department of Surgery, at the [[David Geffen School of Medicine]].<ref name=zaslow/><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1089/rej.2006.9.503 |title=Validated Supercentenarian Cases Aged 114 and Above |year=2006 |last1=Coles |first1=L. Stephen |journal=Rejuvenation Research |volume=9 |issue=4 |pages=503–505 |pmid=17105392 |author2=Los Angeles Gerontology Research Group}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Coles |first=L. Stephen |title=Demographics of Human Supercentenarians and the Implications for Longevity Medicine | date=June 2004 |pages=490–495 |volume=1019 |doi=10.1196/annals.1297.090 |journal=Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences |issue=1 |pmid=15247072|bibcode=2004NYASA1019..490C |s2cid=40216761 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Aging: The Reality |url=http://biomed.gerontologyjournals.org/cgi/content/abstract/59/6/B579 |journal=The Journals of Gerontology: Series A |last=Coles |first=L. Stephen |volume=59 |issue=6 |pages=B579–B586 |doi=10.1093/gerona/59.6.B579 |accessdate=December 29, 2014 |pmid=15215268 |date=June 2004 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090108213303/http://biomed.gerontologyjournals.org/cgi/content/abstract/59/6/B579 |archivedate=January 8, 2009 |doi-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Biography==
Coles was born on January 19, 1941, in [[New York City]]. He received his [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in [[electrical engineering]] from [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]] in [[Troy, New York]], his [[Master's degree|Master's]] in [[mathematics]] from the [[Carnegie Institute of Technology]], and his [[Ph.D.]] in systems and communication sciences from [[Carnegie Mellon University]].<ref name=artificial>{{Cite book |last=Nilsson |first=Nils J. |title=The Quest for Artificial Intelligence |year=2009 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nUJdAAAAQBAJ&q=%22l+stephen+coles%22&pg=PT193 |isbn=978-0521116398}}</ref> After obtaining his [[Doctor of Medicine|M.D.]] at [[Stanford University School of Medicine]], Coles completed his clinical internship in [[obstetrics and gynaecology]] at the [[Jackson Memorial Hospital]] of the [[Miller School of Medicine]] at the [[University of Miami]].<ref name="Coles interview">{{cite journal |title=Interview with L. Stephen Coles, MD, PhD |last=Glaser |first=Vicki |journal=Rejuvenation Research |doi=10.1089/rej.2013.1444 |pmid=23651414 |pages=250–253 |volume=16 |issue=3 |date=June 2013}}</ref>

Coles was treasurer of the [[Supercentenarian Research Foundation]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.foxnews.com/story/supercentenarians-scientists-seek-secret-to-extra-long-life/ |title=Supercentenarians: Scientists Seek Secret to Extra-Long Life |work=Fox News |date=October 6, 2006 |access-date=December 30, 2014}}</ref> as well as co-founder and system administrator of the [[Gerontology Research Group]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Jennifer |last=Medina |title=In Connecticut, World's Oldest Woman Dies at 114. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/01/30/nyregion/30old.html?_r=2 |newspaper=[[New York Times]] |date=January 30, 2007 |accessdate=December 29, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=About the Gerontology Research Group |publisher=GRG.org |url=http://www.grg.org/aboutGRG.html |accessdate=February 22, 2013 |archive-date=January 3, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130103175733/http://www.grg.org/aboutGRG.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Coles died on December 3, 2014, in [[Scottsdale, Arizona]], of [[pancreatic cancer]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Researcher of oldest people dies at 73 |url=http://www.timesargus.com/article/20141205/NEWS04/712059925 |newspaper=[[Times Argus]] |date=December 5, 2014 |accessdate=December 30, 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141208075134/http://www.timesargus.com/article/20141205/NEWS04/712059925 |archivedate=December 8, 2014 }}</ref> His brain was [[cryonics|cryonically preserved]] by [[Alcor Life Extension Foundation]] as their 131st patient.<ref name="LATimes obit">{{Cite news |url=http://www.latimes.com/local/obituaries/la-me-stephen-coles-20141205-story.html |title=L. Stephen Coles dies at 73. studied extreme aging in humans |last=Chawkins |first=Steve |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=December 4, 2014 |accessdate=December 30, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Dr Stephen Coles Becomes Alcor's 131st Patient|url=http://www.alcor.org/blog/dr-stephen-coles-becomes-alcors-131st-patient/|website=Alcor News |date=December 22, 2014 |accessdate=December 29, 2014}}</ref>
